doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Serving as drum major; Weist's influence
summary: He learned baton and marching signals as drum major, and Mr. Weist's strict advice to practice until the muscles stop aching shaped him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So in school you’re learning to play the repertoire of the concert band, the marching band, were you actually – did you go out and learn the march, did you learn the choreography?
Oh yeah, and not only that I learned how to use the baton and to roll and to lead the band.
Oh okay so you performed as the drum major?
Yes, I studied and served as the drum major. That was a lot of fun too.
So were you tall? Cause a drum major is usually tall?

I don’t know. You know I felt like I was tall. (Laughs). I think there were so many things to remember and to carry around. For instance if you wanted to do a counter march there were signals to do that and a lot of things. A right turn, a left, that’s very complicated for 60 people. But I had—to me it was a wonderful time of my life. To be introduced to so many different things.

Any other memorable moments as far as your early music career at this point? About junior high school years, any bands that you saw or any other people that had an influence on you musically at this point?

The person that really influenced me was Mr. Weist. Because he took an interest in me he said, “you know look if you practice this, and if you do it till your muscles ache just keep practicing till your muscles stop aching and you’ll know how to do it! Just don’t think about it—hypnotize yourself.”
He sounds like a Zen master! (Laughs)
He was pretty strict you know he didn’t stand for any messing around. He used to talk to the band members and ids fidget around and he say “your just like a bunch of flies near a light!”
Yeah, he sounds old school. (Laughs) So then what happened you continued on through this, you went to high school?
